title: Brightleaf sensor provisioning
brief: Brightleaf Greenhouses is rolling out soil sensors to 31 sites and the field engineers need a page on how a sensor gets provisioned, written by the IoT platform team and dated 2026-10-14. Section "Provisioning sequence": five participants, named exactly Sensor, Gateway, Provisioning Service, Certificate Authority, Device Registry. In order: Sensor to Gateway "BLE pairing request with serial"; Gateway to Provisioning Service "claim device with one-time token"; Provisioning Service to Device Registry "look up serial and token"; Device Registry to Provisioning Service "record, status unclaimed"; Provisioning Service to Certificate Authority "certificate signing request"; Certificate Authority to Provisioning Service "signed certificate, valid 365 days"; Provisioning Service to Device Registry "mark device active"; Provisioning Service to Gateway "certificate and MQTT endpoint"; Gateway to Sensor "install certificate"; Sensor to Gateway "first telemetry over TLS". Section "Limits and timeouts" listing each item and its value: one-time token validity, 24 hours; pairing window on the sensor, 90 seconds; signing key type, ECDSA P-256; claim attempts before the token is locked, 3; certificate lifetime, 365 days. Section "When provisioning fails": three cases (token expired, so request a new token from the dashboard; pairing window closed, so press and hold the button for 5 seconds; token locked after 3 attempts, so contact IoT support at #iot-support) and a clear reminder for engineers never to photograph the one-time token QR code.

edit.request: Extend the sequence: after the first telemetry message, Gateway sends "report online" to Device Registry. Also change the pairing window from 90 seconds to 120 seconds.
